title: TSMC overseas fabs see profit flip in 1H26
gist: TSMC's Arizona fab swung sharply into the black in 1H2026, with profit up ~663% year over year to NT$36.066 billion and a NT$31.151 billion investment gain (about 2.44% of group net profit), even as ongoing P2 build-out costs pressure earnings and government-subsidy reliance fades.

insights.claim: TSMC's Arizona fab earned NT$4.728 billion (US$148.85 million) in 1H2025 and NT$16.141 billion for full-year 2025, then profit jumped to NT$36.066 billion in 1H2026, up about 663% year over year.
insights.speaker: user nl
insights.so_what: Validates that overseas leading-edge fabs can become strongly profitable, supporting the US expansion thesis.

insights.claim: Because TSMC owns 100% of the Arizona fab, it booked an investment gain of NT$31.151 billion in 1H2026, about 2.44% of its roughly NT$1.28 trillion 1H2026 net profit.
insights.speaker: user nl
insights.so_what: Overseas fab earnings are becoming a measurable contributor to group profit.

insights.claim: Arizona's profitability was helped by tight demand for P1 capacity, higher foundry pricing and gradually easing build-out costs.
insights.speaker: user nl
insights.so_what: Pricing power plus capacity scarcity are the levers turning overseas fabs profitable.

insights.claim: TSMC's Arizona investment gain fell about 13.6% quarter over quarter, from NT$16.909 billion in Q1 2026 to NT$14.603 billion in Q2 2026, indicating depreciation, amortization and operating costs from ongoing P2 construction will keep pressuring earnings.
insights.speaker: user nl
insights.so_what: Overseas fab profitability remains cyclically sensitive to the pace of capacity build-out.

insights.claim: TSMC's combined government support from the US, Germany, Japan and China fell from NT$7.63 billion in 2025 to just NT$590 million in the first half of 2026 as overseas earnings grew.
insights.speaker: user nl
insights.so_what: Declining subsidy dependence suggests overseas operations are becoming self-sustaining.

insights.claim: Under regulatory changes taking effect January 1, 2026, qualifying Arizona investments will earn a 35% tax credit, up from the previous 25%.
insights.speaker: user nl
insights.so_what: Richer US tax credits improve the economics of continued domestic fab investment.
